stories.story: As a returning shopper, I want my saved address pre-filled at checkout so that I can pay without retyping it.
stories.acceptance:
Given a signed-in shopper with a saved address
When they open checkout
Then the address fields are pre-filled and remain editable

Given a signed-in shopper with no saved address
When they open checkout
Then the fields are empty and no error is shown

stories.story: As a shopper, I want the whole checkout on one page so that I can see every step before committing.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper with items in the cart
When they open checkout
Then address, delivery, payment and summary are visible on one page without navigation

Given a section is incomplete
When the shopper tries to pay
Then the first incomplete section is focused and names what is missing
stories.notes: Layout shell only; payment lands in S02.

stories.story: As a first-time shopper, I want to check out without an account so that I am not forced to register.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper who is not signed in
When they open checkout
Then they can enter an email and continue as a guest

Given a guest completes an order
When the confirmation is shown
Then they are offered account creation with the order already attached

stories.story: As a shopper, I want to pay by card so that I can complete my order.
stories.acceptance:
Given a valid test card and a complete address
When the shopper submits payment
Then the order is created and the confirmation page shows the order number

Given the provider returns success
When the webhook arrives
Then the order moves to Paid exactly once, even if the webhook is delivered twice
stories.notes: Provider test mode and published test card numbers only.

stories.story: As a shopper whose card is declined, I want to be told clearly and keep my basket so that I can try another card.
stories.acceptance:
Given a card that the provider declines
When the shopper submits payment
Then a plain-language message names the problem and the basket and address are preserved

Given the provider times out
When no response arrives within the timeout
Then the shopper sees a retry option and no duplicate order is created

stories.story: As a shopper, I want tax and shipping itemised before I pay so that the total holds no surprises.
stories.acceptance:
Given a basket with a delivery address
When the summary renders
Then goods, shipping and tax are listed separately and sum to the displayed total

Given the address changes to another tax jurisdiction
When the shopper updates it
Then tax and total recalculate before payment is enabled

stories.story: As a shopper, I want to enter a promo code so that an advertised discount is applied.
stories.acceptance:
Given a valid, in-date promo code
When the shopper applies it
Then the discount line appears and the total drops accordingly

Given an expired or unknown code
When the shopper applies it
Then the code is rejected with a reason and the total is unchanged

stories.story: As an overseas shopper, I want prices in my own currency so that I know what I am paying.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper in a supported non-home currency
When checkout renders
Then all amounts show in that currency with the rate's as-of timestamp

Given the rate is older than the staleness window
When checkout renders
Then the home currency is shown instead and the event is logged

stories.story: As a shopper, I want my address checked as I type so that delivery does not fail.
stories.acceptance:
Given a partial address
When the shopper pauses typing
Then provider suggestions appear and one can be selected to fill the fields

Given the validation provider is unavailable
When the shopper submits
Then the typed address is accepted and flagged for manual review

stories.story: As a product manager, I want checkout funnel events so that I can see where shoppers drop out.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper moves through checkout
When each step is reached, completed or abandoned
Then a named event with the step and order value is emitted once

Given analytics is blocked by the browser
When events fail to send
Then checkout continues without error

stories.story: As a shopper on a phone, I want checkout usable at mobile width so that I can order on my phone.
stories.acceptance:
Given a 375px viewport
When checkout renders
Then there is no horizontal scroll and every control is reachable with one thumb

Given the on-screen keyboard opens
When a field is focused
Then that field stays visible above the keyboard

stories.story: As a shopper using a keyboard or screen reader, I want to complete checkout unaided so that the service is usable for me.
stories.acceptance:
Given keyboard-only navigation
When the shopper tabs through checkout
Then focus order follows the visual order and focus is always visible

Given a screen reader
When a validation error appears
Then it is announced and programmatically tied to its field
stories.notes: WCAG 2.2 AA on the checkout flow; the wider audit is INI-11.

stories.story: As the team, I want the new checkout behind a flag so that we can roll it back without a deploy.
stories.acceptance:
Given the flag is off
When a shopper opens checkout
Then the legacy checkout is served

Given the flag is on for a percentage of traffic
When it is switched off
Then new sessions fall back to legacy within one minute and in-flight orders still complete

stories.story: As the team, we want the monolith's billing read and write paths mapped so that extraction order is known.
stories.acceptance:
Given the monolith codebase and database
When the spike completes
Then every caller of billing tables is listed with read/write intent and traffic volume

Given the map exists
When the team reviews it
Then the extraction order and the dual-write boundary are agreed and written down
stories.notes: Time-boxed spike. Re-estimate the rest of the epic on its findings.

stories.story: As the team, we want a deployable billing service skeleton so that later stories have somewhere to land.
stories.acceptance:
Given the service repository
When CI runs on main
Then it builds, tests, and deploys to staging with a passing health check

Given the service is deployed
When /health is called
Then it reports version and database connectivity

stories.story: As an internal consumer, I want invoices readable from the billing service so that I can stop querying the monolith.
stories.acceptance:
Given an invoice that exists in the monolith database
When it is fetched from the billing service API
Then the payload matches the monolith's for every field in the contract

Given an unknown invoice id
When it is fetched
Then the service returns 404 with a machine-readable error

stories.story: As the team, we want invoice writes dual-written behind a flag so that we can verify the new store under real traffic.
stories.acceptance:
Given the dual-write flag is on
When an invoice is created in the monolith
Then it is written to both stores and a mismatch raises an alert

Given the billing service is unavailable
When an invoice is created
Then the monolith write still succeeds and the missed write is queued for replay

stories.story: As the team, we want historical invoices backfilled and reconciled so that the new store is complete.
stories.acceptance:
Given the backfill job runs to completion
When the reconciliation report is produced
Then row counts and checksums match per month, and any mismatch is listed by invoice id

Given the job is interrupted
When it is restarted
Then it resumes without duplicating rows

stories.story: As an internal consumer, I want invoice reads served by the billing service so that the monolith stops being the source.
stories.acceptance:
Given the read-cutover flag is on
When any consumer reads an invoice
Then the billing service serves it and p99 latency stays within the agreed budget

Given error rate exceeds the threshold
When the cutover is active
Then traffic reverts to the monolith automatically and the team is paged

stories.story: As the team, we want the monolith's invoice endpoints retired so that there is one source of truth.
stories.acceptance:
Given no caller has used a monolith invoice endpoint for the agreed observation window
When the endpoints are removed
Then the build passes and no consumer errors appear in the following 24 hours

Given a forgotten caller appears
When it calls the removed endpoint
Then it receives 410 Gone with the replacement URL

stories.story: As a subscriber, I want renewals processed by the billing service so that billing no longer depends on the monolith scheduler.
stories.acceptance:
Given a subscription due for renewal
When the billing service job runs
Then exactly one renewal invoice is raised and the payment is attempted once

Given the job runs twice for the same period
When the second run executes
Then it is idempotent and raises no second invoice

stories.story: As a developer, I want the worst flaky tests identified and quarantined so that red builds mean something again.
stories.acceptance:
Given 30 days of CI history
When the flake report runs
Then the 20 highest-flake tests are ranked by failure rate and quarantined from the blocking suite

Given a test is quarantined
When it fails
Then the build still passes and the failure is recorded against its ticket

stories.story: As a developer, I want time-dependent test failures fixed so that the suite passes regardless of when it runs.
stories.acceptance:
Given tests that depend on the current clock, timezone or date boundaries
When they are run with the clock set to a month end, a DST change and a leap day
Then they pass in every case

Given the fixed tests
When run 50 times in CI
Then there are no failures

stories.story: As a developer, I want order-dependent test failures fixed so that tests can run in parallel.
stories.acceptance:
Given tests that share fixtures or global state
When the suite runs in randomised order and in parallel
Then every test passes

Given a test leaks state
When the suite runs
Then the leak is caught by a teardown assertion rather than by a later test failing

stories.story: As a team, we want new flakes caught at the gate so that the backlog does not refill.
stories.acceptance:
Given a dashboard of flake rate by test and by suite
When a newly added test fails intermittently across 20 CI runs
Then it is flagged on the dashboard and the owning team is notified

Given a pull request adds a test that flakes in pre-merge runs
When the gate evaluates it
Then the merge is blocked with the evidence

stories.story: As an on-call engineer, I want a current rotation and escalation runbook so that I know what to do at 3am.
stories.acceptance:
Given the rotation is published
When an alert fires outside working hours
Then the paged engineer and the escalation path after 15 minutes are unambiguous

Given a new joiner takes their first shift
When they follow the runbook
Then they can acknowledge, triage and escalate without asking anyone

stories.story: As an engineering manager, I want a P1 bug SLA dashboard so that breaches are visible before they are complaints.
stories.acceptance:
Given open P1 bugs
When the dashboard refreshes
Then time-to-acknowledge and time-to-fix are shown against the SLA with breaches highlighted

Given a P1 is raised
When the acknowledge target is 30 minutes from being missed
Then the owning team is notified

stories.story: As a customer, I want the standing P1 backlog cleared so that long-broken things get fixed.
stories.acceptance:
Given the P1 bugs open at the start of the sprint
When the sprint ends
Then each is fixed, reclassified with a written reason, or closed as not reproducible

Given a fix ships
When it is verified in production
Then the originating report is updated and closed

stories.story: As an on-call engineer, I want the noisiest alerts fixed or muted so that pages mean something.
stories.acceptance:
Given 30 days of alert history
When the top five noisiest alerts are reviewed
Then each is either made actionable, re-thresholded, or deleted with a reason recorded

Given the changes are live
When the next week's pages are counted
Then out-of-hours pages have fallen against the previous week

stories.story: As a security owner, I want dependencies and patches current so that known vulnerabilities are not left open.
stories.acceptance:
Given the dependency scanner report
When the sweep completes
Then no critical or high advisory older than the agreed window remains unaddressed

Given a patch cannot be applied
When it is deferred
Then the reason, the compensating control and a review date are recorded

stories.story: As a support engineer, I want the most repeated manual request automated so that toil stops growing.
stories.acceptance:
Given the support request log for the quarter
When the most frequent manual request is automated as self-service
Then a requester can complete it without engineering involvement

Given the automation fails
When it errors
Then the requester sees a clear message and the old manual path still works

stories.story: As a service owner, I want SLOs and error-budget alerts so that reliability is measured, not asserted.
stories.acceptance:
Given the agreed SLIs for availability and latency
When the error budget burn rate exceeds the fast-burn threshold
Then the owning team is alerted with the contributing endpoints

Given a month closes
When the SLO report is produced
Then budget consumed and remaining are stated per service

stories.story: As a support engineer, I want handoff docs for the new billing service so that I can support it without the authors.
stories.acceptance:
Given the billing service is serving reads
When support receives a billing question
Then the runbook names the dashboards, the common failure modes and their first-line remedies

Given an unfamiliar error
When support follows the escalation section
Then the owning team and the required diagnostic bundle are named

stories.story: As a compliance owner, I want a quarterly access review so that access matches current roles.
stories.acceptance:
Given the access list for production systems
When the review completes
Then every entitlement is confirmed by the system owner or removed, and the evidence is retained

Given a leaver is found with live access
When the review runs
Then access is revoked the same day and the gap is recorded

stories.story: As a team, we want incident retro actions closed so that the same incident does not recur.
stories.acceptance:
Given the retro actions raised this quarter
When the sprint ends
Then each is done or has a named owner and a date, with none silently dropped

Given an action is overdue by more than one sprint
When the review runs
Then it is escalated to the manager with the risk restated

stories.story: As a returning shopper, I want my card saved securely so that I need not re-enter it.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper who opts to save their card
When the order completes
Then only the provider token is stored and the card number never reaches our systems

Given a saved card has expired
When checkout renders
Then it is shown as expired and cannot be selected

stories.story: As a repeat buyer, I want to reorder a past order in one click so that routine purchases take seconds.
stories.acceptance:
Given a past order whose items are all still available
When the shopper chooses Reorder
Then the basket is filled and checkout opens with the previous address and payment selected

Given an item is discontinued
When Reorder runs
Then the available items are added and the missing ones are listed

stories.story: As a shopper with several addresses, I want to pick from an address book so that I can send orders elsewhere.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper with two or more saved addresses
When checkout renders
Then each is selectable and the default is pre-selected

Given an address is edited during checkout
When the order completes
Then the change is saved against the address book, not just the order

stories.story: As a shopper, I want to split payment across two methods so that I can combine a gift card with a card.
stories.acceptance:
Given a basket and a gift card with partial balance
When the shopper applies the gift card and a card
Then the gift card is drawn down first and the card covers the remainder

Given the second payment fails
When the order is submitted
Then the gift card draw-down is reversed and no order is created

stories.story: As a mobile shopper, I want to pay with a digital wallet so that I can check out without typing.
stories.acceptance:
Given a device with a wallet configured
When the shopper chooses wallet payment
Then the sheet opens pre-filled and a successful authorisation creates the order

Given the wallet is unavailable on the device
When checkout renders
Then the option is hidden rather than shown failing

stories.story: As a gift buyer, I want to add a message and delivery instructions so that the parcel arrives as intended.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper adds a gift message within the length limit
When the order is placed
Then the message appears on the packing slip and not on the invoice

Given instructions exceed the courier's field length
When the shopper types
Then the limit is enforced with a visible counter

stories.story: As a regular customer, I want to set up a recurring order at checkout so that I stop reordering manually.
stories.acceptance:
Given a basket eligible for subscription
When the shopper selects a delivery interval
Then a subscription is created and the first order is placed immediately

Given the shopper cancels before the next cycle
When the cycle date arrives
Then no order and no charge are raised

stories.story: As a shopper, I want to choose a delivery slot so that I am home when it arrives.
stories.acceptance:
Given a postcode with slot availability
When checkout renders
Then the next available slots are shown with any surcharge stated

Given the chosen slot sells out before submission
When the order is placed
Then the shopper is asked to re-pick and is not charged the surcharge twice

stories.story: As a merchandiser, I want a post-purchase offer slot so that confirmation pages earn their traffic.
stories.acceptance:
Given a completed order
When the confirmation page renders
Then one relevant offer is shown and its impressions and clicks are logged

Given no relevant offer exists
When the page renders
Then the slot collapses without leaving empty space

stories.story: As the team, we want a written parity gap list so that mobile work is scoped from evidence.
stories.acceptance:
Given the web and mobile checkout flows
When the audit completes
Then every gap is listed with its user impact and an estimate

Given the list is agreed
When the epic is re-planned
Then the remaining stories cover every gap marked must-have
stories.notes: Time-boxed. Re-estimate the epic on its findings.

stories.story: As a mobile shopper, I want saved addresses and wallet payment in the app so that checkout matches the web.
stories.acceptance:
Given a signed-in app user with a saved address and wallet
When they open checkout in the app
Then both are available and pre-selected as on the web

Given the app is offline at checkout
When payment is attempted
Then a clear offline message is shown and the basket is preserved

stories.story: As a mobile shopper, I want order status pushed to my phone so that I need not check the app.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shopper who has granted notification permission
When the order ships or is delivered
Then a push arrives once per event with the order reference

Given permission is denied
When the event occurs
Then no push is attempted and in-app status still updates

stories.story: As a mobile shopper, I want a notification to open the right screen so that I am not dropped on the home page.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shipping notification for a specific order
When the shopper taps it
Then the app opens that order's detail screen, installing state permitting

Given the app is not installed
When the link is followed
Then the mobile web order page opens instead

stories.story: As a mobile shopper on a poor connection, I want my basket kept so that I do not lose my selections.
stories.acceptance:
Given items added while offline
When connectivity returns
Then the basket syncs without duplicating lines

Given the same account adds items on web and app while offline
When both sync
Then the merge is deterministic and the shopper is told what changed

stories.story: As a mobile shopper, I want promo codes to work in the app so that advertised offers apply everywhere.
stories.acceptance:
Given a valid promo code
When entered in the app
Then the same discount applies as on the web

Given a web-only code
When entered in the app
Then it is rejected with the reason stated

stories.story: As a mobile shopper, I want biometric sign-in so that I can return without typing a password.
stories.acceptance:
Given a device with biometrics enrolled
When the shopper opts in
Then later launches authenticate biometrically and no password is stored on device

Given biometric authentication fails three times
When the shopper retries
Then password sign-in is offered

stories.story: As a release manager, I want a staged app rollout so that a bad build reaches few users.
stories.acceptance:
Given a release candidate
When it is published
Then it goes to a small percentage first and crash-free rate is monitored against the threshold

Given the threshold is breached
When the rollout is halted
Then the previous version remains available to new installs

stories.story: As an engineer, I want structured logs with trace ids so that I can follow one request end to end.
stories.acceptance:
Given a request entering any service
When it is logged
Then the entry is JSON with a trace id propagated to downstream calls

Given a log search by trace id
When it runs
Then every hop of that request is returned in order

stories.story: As a data protection owner, I want logs scrubbed and expiring so that we do not hoard personal data.
stories.acceptance:
Given a log line containing an email, card fragment or token
When it is written
Then the value is redacted at source

Given the retention window passes
When the lifecycle job runs
Then the entries are deleted and the deletion is auditable

stories.story: As an engineer, I want tracing across checkout and billing so that latency can be attributed.
stories.acceptance:
Given a checkout request that calls the billing service
When the trace is viewed
Then each span shows its duration and the slowest hop is identifiable

Given a downstream call fails
When the trace is viewed
Then the error and its span are marked

stories.story: As a platform owner, I want sampling configurable per route so that tracing cost stays bounded.
stories.acceptance:
Given a high-traffic route
When its sampling rate is lowered
Then trace volume drops accordingly without code changes

Given an error response
When sampling would drop it
Then it is retained regardless of rate

stories.story: As a service owner, I want an SLO dashboard per service so that reliability is visible at a glance.
stories.acceptance:
Given the agreed availability and latency SLIs
When the dashboard loads
Then current compliance, budget consumed and budget remaining are shown per service

Given a service has no SLO defined
When the dashboard loads
Then it is listed as unmeasured rather than omitted

stories.story: As an on-call engineer, I want burn-rate alerts so that I am paged before the budget is gone.
stories.acceptance:
Given a fast burn of the error budget
When the threshold is crossed
Then on-call is paged with the service and contributing endpoints

Given a slow burn
When the threshold is crossed
Then a ticket is raised instead of a page

stories.story: As an engineering manager, I want the P1 SLA held through Q2 so that reliability work does not slip.
stories.acceptance:
Given P1 bugs raised during the quarter
When the quarter closes
Then the acknowledge and fix targets were met for the agreed percentage

Given a breach occurs
When it is reviewed
Then the cause is recorded and an action is raised

stories.story: As a security owner, I want the Q2 patch sweep done so that advisories do not accumulate.
stories.acceptance:
Given the scanner report at sweep time
When the sweep completes
Then no critical or high advisory beyond the agreed age remains open

Given a patch breaks a test
When it is held back
Then the reason and review date are recorded

stories.story: As an on-call engineer, I want shift reports generated so that handover is not from memory.
stories.acceptance:
Given a shift ends
When the report is generated
Then pages, their resolutions and open follow-ups are listed automatically

Given nothing happened
When the shift ends
Then a quiet-shift report is still produced

stories.story: As an on-call engineer, I want the top alerts' runbooks current so that I am not guessing.
stories.acceptance:
Given the three most frequent alerts
When each runbook is reviewed
Then the steps match the current system and were executed once to confirm

Given a runbook step is obsolete
When it is found
Then it is corrected or deleted rather than left

stories.story: As a support engineer, I want the second most common request automated so that toil keeps falling.
stories.acceptance:
Given the quarter's request log
When the second most frequent manual request is automated
Then requesters can self-serve it without engineering

Given the automation errors
When it fails
Then the manual path still works and the failure is logged

stories.story: As a developer, I want dead feature flags removed so that the code stops branching on history.
stories.acceptance:
Given flags fully rolled out or abandoned for over 90 days
When the cleanup runs
Then the flag and its dead branch are deleted and tests still pass

Given a flag is still referenced
When cleanup is attempted
Then it is skipped and reported

stories.story: As a team, we want Q2 retro actions closed so that incidents teach us something.
stories.acceptance:
Given retro actions raised in the quarter
When it closes
Then each is done or has an owner and a date

Given an action is overdue a full sprint
When the review runs
Then it is escalated with the risk restated

stories.story: As a compliance owner, I want the Q2 access review completed so that entitlements match roles.
stories.acceptance:
Given the production access list
When the review completes
Then every entitlement is confirmed or revoked with evidence retained

Given a leaver still has access
When found
Then it is revoked the same day and recorded

stories.story: As a service owner, I want a restore drill so that backups are known to work.
stories.acceptance:
Given the latest backup
When it is restored to an isolated environment
Then integrity checks pass and the restore time is recorded against the RTO

Given the restore fails
When the drill ends
Then a P1 is raised against the backup system

stories.story: As an enterprise admin, I want SAML single sign-on so that my staff use our own identity provider.
stories.acceptance:
Given exchanged SAML metadata with one IdP
When a user authenticates there
Then a session is created with identity mapped from the assertion

Given an assertion is expired, unsigned or replayed
When it is presented
Then authentication is refused and the attempt is logged

stories.story: As an enterprise user, I want sign-in to work from either side so that I can start at our portal or yours.
stories.acceptance:
Given an IdP-initiated login
When the user clicks the app tile
Then they land signed in on the app home page

Given an SP-initiated login
When the user enters their work email
Then they are redirected to the right IdP by domain

stories.story: As an enterprise admin, I want users provisioned automatically so that onboarding needs no tickets.
stories.acceptance:
Given SCIM is configured
When a user is assigned the app in the IdP
Then the account is created with the mapped attributes within the agreed interval

Given an attribute changes in the IdP
When SCIM syncs
Then the account is updated and not duplicated

stories.story: As a security owner, I want deprovisioning to cut access immediately so that leavers lose it at once.
stories.acceptance:
Given a user is unassigned or deactivated in the IdP
When SCIM syncs
Then the account is disabled and existing sessions and tokens are revoked

Given SCIM is unreachable
When the sync window is missed
Then an alert is raised rather than failing silently

stories.story: As an enterprise admin, I want IdP groups mapped to roles so that permissions follow our directory.
stories.acceptance:
Given a mapping from IdP groups to application roles
When a user signs in
Then their roles match their current group membership

Given a user is in no mapped group
When they sign in
Then they get the configured default role and the gap is logged

stories.story: As an enterprise admin, I want to configure and test SSO myself so that setup needs no support ticket.
stories.acceptance:
Given an admin on the SSO settings page
When they paste metadata and run Test connection
Then the result states success or the precise failure

Given a misconfiguration is saved
When existing users sign in
Then the previous working config stays active until the test passes

stories.story: As a platform owner, I want a break-glass local login so that an IdP outage does not lock everyone out.
stories.acceptance:
Given SSO is enforced and the IdP is unreachable
When a designated break-glass admin signs in locally with MFA
Then access is granted and every use is alerted and audited

Given a non-designated user attempts it
When they try
Then it is refused

stories.story: As the team, we want the target schema and migration order agreed so that the move is not improvised.
stories.acceptance:
Given the current warehouse and its consumers
When the spike completes
Then the target schema, the migration order and the cutover criteria are written down

Given the plan is reviewed
When risks are listed
Then each has a mitigation or an explicit acceptance
stories.notes: Time-boxed spike; re-estimate the epic afterwards.

stories.story: As a data engineer, I want one source ingesting into the new platform so that the pipeline is proven end to end.
stories.acceptance:
Given the landing zone exists
When the first source's daily load runs
Then rows arrive partitioned and typed as designed, with failures alerting

Given a malformed batch
When it is ingested
Then it is quarantined without blocking the rest

stories.story: As an analyst, I want history backfilled so that trends do not start at the migration date.
stories.acceptance:
Given the agreed history window
When the backfill completes
Then partitions exist for every period with row counts matching the source per month

Given the backfill is interrupted
When restarted
Then it resumes without duplicating partitions

stories.story: As a data engineer, I want an automated parity check so that drift is caught early.
stories.acceptance:
Given both platforms are loaded for the same day
When the parity job runs
Then row counts and key checksums are compared and differences are reported by table

Given a mismatch exceeds the threshold
When the job finishes
Then the owning team is alerted

stories.story: As an analyst, I want the reporting models rebuilt so that dashboards have something to read.
stories.acceptance:
Given the core reporting models
When they are rebuilt on the new platform
Then each returns the same results as the old for a sampled date range

Given a model cannot match
When the difference is investigated
Then the cause is documented and signed off or fixed

stories.story: As a data owner, I want both pipelines run in parallel with a diff report so that cutover is evidence-based.
stories.acceptance:
Given both pipelines running daily
When the diff report is produced
Then per-table differences are listed with severity

Given the report is clean for the agreed number of consecutive days
When cutover is proposed
Then the criteria are demonstrably met

stories.story: As an analyst, I want dashboards pointed at the new platform so that there is one place to look.
stories.acceptance:
Given the cutover criteria are met
When dashboards are repointed
Then each loads within its latency budget and figures match the last parallel-run day

Given a dashboard breaks
When it is found
Then it can be repointed back within the day

stories.story: As a platform owner, I want the old pipeline decommissioned so that we stop paying twice.
stories.acceptance:
Given dashboards and consumers are on the new platform
When the old pipeline is disabled
Then no consumer errors appear for the agreed observation window and the cost drop is visible

Given a forgotten consumer surfaces
